title: Machiavelli Got This Right
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Admired Leadership argues that, whatever Machiavelli got wrong about fear, he was right that the people around a leader reveal the leader. People judge a leader's quality and competence by whom they spend time with, delegate to and seek counsel from. The piece adds that what direct reports do and say is presumed to be endorsed by the leader, and that a leader's inner circle is read as a statement of values. The move is to turn a historical observation into a practical audit: leaders should make sure the team and kitchen cabinet reflect their values and offer the broadest range of perspectives. It ends with two questions for the reader about what their own lieutenants say about them.
points: Whom a leader spends time with, delegates to and consults is the main evidence people use to judge that leader.
Key lieutenants are symbols of what the leader values, and their competence and character reflect directly on the leader.
Leaders are presumed to know and endorse what their direct reports do, so claiming ignorance is never accepted.
The tighter the inner circle, the more it is read as standing for the leader's values.
The best leaders curate that circle so it reflects their values while offering the widest range of perspectives.
quotes: He argued that the people surrounding a leader tell others a lot about that leader.
We largely judge the quality and competence of a leader by who they spend time with, who they delegate important assignments to, and who they seek advice and counsel from.
The competence, character, and talent of those on the leadership team are a direct reflection of the leader and what they stand for.

The idea that a leader doesn’t know or is unaware of what their direct reports do or how they interact with others is never accepted. Whatever those closest to the leader do and say is viewed as coming directly from the leader.
The best leaders are mindful of this and work hard to ensure this group accurately reflects their values and offers the broadest possible range of perspectives and insights.
What do the team members surrounding you say about you and your leadership? How well do your key lieutenants represent what you stand for?
